# window


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

A native window over a loopback server, and the menus around it.

pywebview is imported inside the functions that need it, never at module
scope. Importing `kavacha.window` on a machine with no window costs
nothing, and the parts that decide something run anywhere: the readiness
check, the URL wait, the size parsing, the splash, the chord table.

The Dock, the menu bar and the text-substitution defaults are macOS.
[`menus`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#menus),
[`quiet_text_substitution`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#quiet_text_substitution),
[`keep_running_in_dock`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#keep_running_in_dock)
and
[`watch_open_events`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#watch_open_events)
check `sys.platform` first and answer `[]`, False or None off darwin.
[`dock_menu`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#dock_menu),
[`_decorate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#_decorate)
and the two Objective-C classes do not check, and are reached only from
a caller that does.

Every failure here is printed and swallowed. A missing inline browser, a
menu bar that will not build, a window that will not come back: the app
runs without them.
[`run_shell`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#run_shell)
is the exception, and it raises before it opens anything.

[`backend`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/probe.html#backend),
[`shell_ready`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/probe.html#shell_ready)
and
[`wait_for_http`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/probe.html#wait_for_http)
also exist in `probe`. The two
[`wait_for_http`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/probe.html#wait_for_http)
differ, and the difference is in the section below.

`APP_NAME` and `CFG` are read from the environment once, at import. A
host that wants its own name or its own configuration directory sets
`$KAVACHA_APP_NAME` or `$KAVACHA_CFG` before importing this module.
Setting either afterwards changes nothing.

Reading them creates nothing on disk.

### errstr

``` python
def errstr(
    e
):
```

*Call self as a function.*

[`errstr`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#errstr)
names the exception type as well as its message, and every printed
failure in this module goes through it. A `KeyError` prints its key and
nothing else, an `ImportError` names a module and not what wanted it,
and several of these exceptions carry an empty message. The type is what
makes the printed line worth reading.

``` python
errstr(ValueError('port 9223 is in use')), errstr(KeyError('cocoa'))
```

    ('ValueError: port 9223 is in use', "KeyError: 'cocoa'")

`DEFAULT_SIZE` is the size a window opens at. `MIN_SIZE` is two things:
the floor
[`window_size`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#window_size)
enforces on a requested size, and the `min_size` every window is built
with, so the size a user can drag a window down to is the size the app
is willing to open at.

`STORAGE` is the web engine’s own profile: cookies, local storage, and
whatever else it keeps between runs. It sits inside `CFG`.
[`make_window`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#make_window)
creates it, and that is the only directory this module creates.

`EAGER_CDP` is the name of the environment variable
[`warm_cdp`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#warm_cdp)
reads, not its value.

``` python
DEFAULT_SIZE, MIN_SIZE, str(STORAGE).replace(str(CFG), '/cfg')   # the config directory stands in
```

    ((1440, 900), (900, 560), '/cfg/webview')

### ShellApi

``` python
def ShellApi(
    *args, **kwargs
):
```

*What the page may ask the native window for, as
`window.pywebview.api.*`.*

[`ShellApi`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#shellapi)
is the whole of what the page may ask the native window for. pywebview
exposes each public method as `window.pywebview.api.<name>` and calls it
on a thread of its own, so nothing here may assume the main thread.

`on_open_folder` and `on_recent` belong to the host and are set by
[`run_shell`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#run_shell).
Until they are set, `open_folder` returns False and `recent` returns an
empty list. An empty path returns False without calling the host.

`open_folder` returns once the host has been called. True says the
request was accepted, not that a window appeared:
[`run_shell`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#run_shell)
wraps the host’s callback so the work leaves the calling thread
immediately.

`recent` returns a list, whatever the host’s callback returns. The page
is given a JSON array either way.

`pick_folder` is the platform’s own folder chooser and is the one method
that needs pywebview. It returns None when there is no active window,
when the chooser was cancelled, and when the chooser raised. Nothing on
this page exercises it.

``` python
api = ShellApi()
opened = []
api.on_open_folder = opened.append
api.open_folder('/proj/demo'), api.open_folder(''), opened
```

    (True, False, ['/proj/demo'])

### shell_ready

``` python
def shell_ready(
    platform:NoneType=None
):
```

*`(ok, why)`: whether a native window can be opened here, and what is
missing if not.*

A platform absent from `BACKENDS` has no native window here.
[`shell_ready`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/probe.html#shell_ready)
answers that case and the missing-pywebview case in one pair. `ok` is
False for both and `why` says which it was. When `ok` is True, `why` is
the pywebview GUI name, which
[`run_shell`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#run_shell)
passes on as `gui`.

Importing `webview` is how
[`shell_ready`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/probe.html#shell_ready)
finds out. The `ImportError` is the answer rather than a failure, and
this is the only place the module decides whether a window is possible.

``` python
backend('darwin'), backend('win32'), backend('plan9')
```

    ('cocoa', 'edgechromium', None)

``` python
test_eq(shell_ready('plan9'), (False, 'no native webview backend for plan9'))
ok, why = shell_ready('darwin')
test_eq(ok, why == 'cocoa')   # the gui name when a window can be opened, what is missing when not
```

### wait_for_http

``` python
def wait_for_http(
    url, timeout:int=60, interval:float=0.1
):
```

*Block until `url` answers, or `timeout` passes. True if the server came
up.*

[`wait_for_http`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/probe.html#wait_for_http)
polls until the server answers or `timeout` passes. It never raises, and
False means the timeout passed.

An error status is an answer. A 4xx proves something is listening on the
port, which is the question being asked, so a workspace whose root is
not routed yet is not waited out for a minute. `probe.wait_for_http`
treats a 404 as a not-yet instead, and the two are not interchangeable.

Every other exception is a not-yet. A connection refused while the
server is still binding its port is the ordinary case, not a failure.

``` python
wait_for_http(url), wait_for_http(url + 'missing', timeout=.3)   # a 404 proves the port is live
```

    (True, True)

### warm_cdp

``` python
def warm_cdp(
    port:int=9223, profile:NoneType=None
):
```

*Start Chrome at launch only if `$KAVACHA_CDP_EAGER` asks for it. See
`docs/desktop.md`.*

The inline browser is a Chrome the host drives over CDP, brought up by
`fossick`.
[`start_cdp`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#start_cdp)
boots it on a daemon thread and returns that thread. Nothing about the
window depends on it. fossick absent, Chrome absent or a boot that fails
prints one line and the app carries on without an inline browser.
`wait=True` joins the thread, bounded by `timeout`, or by 30 seconds
when there is none.

[`warm_cdp`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#warm_cdp)
is the call made at launch. It starts nothing unless
`$KAVACHA_CDP_EAGER` is `1`, `true` or `yes`. The value is stripped
before it is compared and the comparison is case-sensitive, so `TRUE` is
not one of them. Anything else, including an unset variable, returns
None and boots no thread.

### window_size

``` python
def window_size(
    spec:NoneType=None
):
```

*`WIDTHxHEIGHT` from `spec` or `$KAVACHA_WINDOW_SIZE`, else the
default.*

[`window_size`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#window_size)
reads `WIDTHxHEIGHT` from `spec`, or from `$KAVACHA_WINDOW_SIZE` when
`spec` is empty. The separator is matched in either case.

A size below `MIN_SIZE` in either dimension is refused, and so is
anything that will not parse. Both give `DEFAULT_SIZE`. Nothing raises
and nothing warns, so a mistyped variable opens the default window
rather than no window.

``` python
window_size('1600x1000'), window_size('1280X800'), window_size('320x200'), window_size('wide')
```

    ((1600, 1000), (1280, 800), (1440, 900), (1440, 900))

The splash is inline HTML referring to nothing outside itself, so a
window has something to show before any server exists and asks the
network for nothing while it waits.

[`_unreachable`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#_unreachable)
is the same page with the waiting line replaced by the address that did
not answer, in red. A window whose server never came up says which
address failed rather than showing an empty frame.

``` python
_unreachable('http://127.0.0.1:8000/').splitlines()[-1]
```

    '<div><b>leela</b><i style="color:#e06c75">the workspace at http://127.0.0.1:8000/ did not answer</i></div>'

### dock_menu

``` python
def dock_menu(
    on_folder, recent:NoneType=None
):
```

*The Dock’s own menu: the folders last open, newest first. `recent` is
the host’s list of paths.*

The Dock menu is the folders last open, at most `DOCK_RECENT` of them,
in the order the host gave them. Nothing here sorts the list. The limit
is what keeps the menu a shortcut rather than a file browser.

A row is titled by the folder’s own name: the basename with a trailing
separator removed, and the whole path when that leaves nothing, which is
the case for `/`. The full path is both the tooltip and the represented
object, and the represented object is what comes back when the row
fires.

An empty list still gives a menu. It holds one disabled row, so the Dock
menu never looks broken.

`_dock_target` is built once and kept for the life of the process. An
`NSMenuItem` holds no strong reference to a Python object, so a target
kept nowhere else is collected and its rows do nothing.

Every function here needs AppKit. Nothing on this page exercises them.

Closing the last window hides it rather than quitting, so the app stays
in the Dock. `windowShouldClose_` orders the window out and answers NO.
Clicking the Dock icon with no window visible orders the most recently
hidden one back in. Cmd+Q still quits.

`_hidden` is a stack, and a window closed twice is moved to the top of
it rather than listed twice.

The two delegate classes are built on first use and kept in
`_delegates`. An Objective-C class name is global to the runtime, so a
second definition of either is an error rather than a second class.

`_on_folder` is module state because `applicationDockMenu_` is handed
nothing but the application.
[`keep_running_in_dock`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#keep_running_in_dock)
sets it.

Both subclasses derive from pywebview’s cocoa `BrowserView` delegates,
so
[`_dock_delegates`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#_dock_delegates)
cannot be built on this page.

[`quiet_text_substitution`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#quiet_text_substitution)

### keep_running_in_dock

``` python
def keep_running_in_dock(
    on_folder:NoneType=None
):
```

*Hide the last window rather than quit, and fill the Dock menu. Reopen
shows one window. Cmd+Q quits.*

[`keep_running_in_dock`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#keep_running_in_dock)
replaces pywebview’s two delegate classes. It has an effect only before
any window is built, which is why
[`run_shell`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#run_shell)
calls it before the first
[`make_window`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#make_window).

It returns False and prints when pywebview’s cocoa backend cannot be
imported. `_on_folder` is set after that import succeeds, so a failed
call leaves nothing half-installed.

`WINDOW_KW` is what every window is built with. The title and the size
are the two things a caller may vary and are not in it, so a window
opened at launch and one opened for a folder an hour later are the same
window.

`min_size` is `MIN_SIZE`, the floor
[`window_size`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#window_size)
enforces.

``` python
WINDOW_KW
```

### off_main_thread

``` python
def off_main_thread(
    fn, name:str='kavacha-shell'
):
```

*Run `fn(arg)` on a thread of its own; `create_window` builds nothing on
the main thread.*

[`off_main_thread`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#off_main_thread)
wraps a one-argument callback so that calling it starts a thread and
returns. Every native caller reaches Python on the main thread: a Dock
menu row, an Apple Event, a `js_api` call. None of them may build a
window there, because the main thread is inside the GUI loop.
[`run_shell`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#run_shell)
wraps the host’s open-folder callback once and passes the wrapper to
everything that can open a folder.

The wrapper returns None. Nothing comes back, and an exception inside
`fn` ends its own thread and reaches no caller.

`name` is the thread name, which is what a stack dump shows.

``` python
seen, done = [], Event()
go = off_main_thread(lambda p: (seen.append((p, threading.current_thread().name)), done.set()))
go('/proj/demo'); done.wait(5)
seen
```

    [('/proj/demo', 'kavacha-shell')]

### open_window

``` python
def open_window(
    url, title:str='app', key:NoneType=None, url_wait:int=90
):
```

*A window on `url`, raised rather than opened twice when `key` already
has one.*

[`open_window`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#open_window)
with a `key` that already has a window raises that window instead of
opening a second one. cocoa answers `show` with a `callAfter`, so any
thread may ask. A window that will not come back prints and is returned
anyway, because there is no better window to give the caller.

Without a `key` there is no bookkeeping and every call opens a window.

[`_point`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#_point)
waits for the server and then loads the URL. A server that has not
answered within `url_wait` leaves the window on
[`_unreachable`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#_unreachable),
naming the address.
[`_point`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#_point)
never leaves a window on the splash.

``` python
_windows['demo'], _windows['gone'] = _Win(), _Win(fail=True)
u = 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/'
open_window(u, 'Demo', key='demo').calls, open_window(u, 'Notes', key='gone').calls
```

      could not raise the window for Notes: RuntimeError: the window is gone

    (['show'], [])

### run_shell

``` python
def run_shell(
    urls, titles:tuple=(), url_wait:int=90, gui:NoneType=None, icon:NoneType=None, size:NoneType=None,
    on_ready:NoneType=None, on_open_folder:NoneType=None, keys:tuple=()
):
```

*One native window per workspace URL, until they all close. Blocks, on
the main thread.*

[`run_shell`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#run_shell)
is the desktop entry point. It opens one window per workspace URL,
starts the GUI loop, and blocks until every window is closed. It has to
be called on the main thread.

It refuses before it builds anything. A platform with no backend, or a
missing pywebview, raises `RuntimeError` carrying the reason
[`shell_ready`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/probe.html#shell_ready)
gave. An empty `urls` raises `ValueError`.

`titles` and `keys` are padded to the length of `urls`, so a caller may
name the first window and leave the rest.

The order on darwin is fixed. Text substitution is turned off before a
web view can ask for it, and the delegates are replaced before any
window takes one.

One menu bar list is built and shared by every window. pywebview
rebuilds the bar whenever the focused window’s menu is not the one it
built last, and a window opened for a folder later has no menu of its
own.

The URL wait happens inside `load`, which pywebview calls once the GUI
loop is up. A server that takes a minute to start still puts a window on
screen at once.

### menus

``` python
def menus():
```

*The menu bar, or an empty bar off macOS. Its own function so a test can
build one.*

[`menus`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#menus)
returns an empty list off darwin, and an empty list when any part of

### watch_open_events

``` python
def watch_open_events(
    on_folder
):
```

*Answer the `odoc` Apple Event Finder sends a running app. macOS only,
best-effort.*

Finder sends a running application an `odoc` Apple Event when a folder
is dropped on its Dock icon or opened with it. An application that
registers no handler is sent the event and drops it, and nothing opens.

[`watch_open_events`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#watch_open_events)
registers one and returns the handler, so a caller can invoke it
directly. It returns None off darwin, when Foundation will not import,
and when registration fails.

The handler passes on only paths that are directories on this machine. A
`file:` URL is converted through `NSURL`, and anything else is taken as
a path already. An event it cannot read prints and is dropped.

`_RecentTarget` and `_OpenHandler` are Objective-C classes, defined at
import where pyobjc is present and bound to None where it is not. The
class body runs at import, so any failure inside it, not only a missing
pyobjc, leaves both names None. Every caller of either is behind a
`sys.platform` check.

`CMD`, `CTRL`, `ALT` and `SHIFT` are AppKit’s `NSEventModifierFlag`
bits, written out rather than read from AppKit so that a chord can be
built on any machine.

`_MODS` is the spelling the host’s keymap uses. `mod` and `cmd` are one
bit: `mod` is the portable name for the platform’s own modifier, and on
macOS that is Command. `opt` and `alt` are one bit. `hyper` is all four.

`_NAMED` maps the key names a keymap uses to the single characters
AppKit expects. The arrows and the page, home, end and delete keys are
private-use characters, which is how AppKit spells them. The rest are
control characters.

### mac_key

``` python
def mac_key(
    chord
):
```

*`(keyEquivalent, modifierMask)` for one chord, or None when AppKit
cannot spell it.*

[`mac_key`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#mac_key)
turns one chord into the pair an `NSMenuItem` wants. None means AppKit
cannot spell it, and the row is left with no key equivalent rather than
a wrong one.

Only the first stroke is read. A keymap entry written as a sequence,
with a space between strokes, has no key equivalent, and its first
stroke is what AppKit can install.

A single uppercase base carries its own shift, so `mod+P` and
`mod+shift+p` give the same pair. The base is lowercased afterwards:
AppKit takes the shift in the modifier mask and the unshifted character
as the key.

None comes back for a modifier name that is not in `_MODS`, and for a
base that is not one character after `_NAMED` is applied. `f5` is the
ordinary case of the second.

``` python
mac_key('mod+p'), mac_key('mod+f5'), mac_key('meta+p')
```

    (('p', 1048576), None, None)

``` python
test_eq(mac_key('mod+P'), mac_key('mod+shift+p'))        # an uppercase base carries the shift itself
test_eq(mac_key('hyper+k'), ('k', CMD | CTRL | ALT | SHIFT))
test_eq(mac_key('mod+k mod+s'), mac_key('mod+k'))        # a sequence installs its first stroke
```

### menu_chord

``` python
def menu_chord(
    action, lookup
):
```

*The chord to put on a menu row, or None to leave it bare.*

A key equivalent is consulted before the keystroke reaches the web view,
so anything installed here is taken away from the page. Only a global
action with a modifier is safe: a scoped one would fire outside its
scope, and a bare letter would fire while you were typing it.

A key equivalent is consulted before the keystroke reaches the web view,
so every chord installed on a menu row is taken away from the page.
[`menu_chord`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#menu_chord)
is the filter that decides which may be taken.

Three things have to hold. The action is bound, its scope is `global`,
and its first stroke carries a modifier. A scoped action would fire
outside its scope. A bare letter would fire while you were typing it.

`lookup` is the host’s keymap, as a callable from an action to a
[\[`Binding`\](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#binding)](menus.html)
or `None`. kavacha ships no keymap of its own, so a plain dict’s `get`
is a lookup and is what the examples here use.

``` python
KEYS = {'save':         Binding(('mod+s',), 'Save'),
        'quick_open':   Binding(('mod+shift+o',)),
        'find_in_file': Binding(('mod+f',), 'Find', scope='editor'),
        'comment':      Binding(('/',), 'Comment'),
        'orphan':       Binding()}
{a: menu_chord(a, KEYS.get) for a in ('save', 'quick_open', 'find_in_file', 'comment', 'orphan')}
```

    {'save': ('s', 1048576),
     'quick_open': ('o', 1179648),
     'find_in_file': None,
     'comment': None,
     'orphan': None}

`save` is global, bound and modified, so it earns its chord. The other
three are each refused for a different reason, and an action the keymap
has never heard of is refused too.

[`_title`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#_title)
prefers the keymap’s label. Without one it opens up the action’s
underscores, so a row is never blank and never shows a bare identifier.

``` python
_title(MenuItem('save'), KEYS.get), _title(MenuItem('quick_open'), KEYS.get)
```

    ('Save', 'Quick open')

### menu_bar

``` python
def menu_bar(
    bar, lookup, on_action, run:NoneType=None
):
```

*pywebview menus for `bar`, plus the table
[`_decorate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#_decorate)
needs to finish them off AppKit-side.*

[`menu_bar`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#menu_bar)
walks `bar`, the host’s menu table, and returns pywebview `Menu` objects
together with the table
[`_decorate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#_decorate)
needs afterwards. That table is keyed by `(menu title, row title)`,
because a title is all AppKit gives back when the bar is rebuilt.

There are three kinds of row. A
[`MenuItem`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#menuitem)
with no action is a separator. A
[`Js`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#js) row runs its
expression through
[`run`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/build.html#run). Anything
else calls `on_action` with the action name, under the label the keymap
gives it.

A [`Std`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#std) row is
one AppKit implements itself, so the callback built here does nothing.
[`_decorate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#_decorate)
gives the row a nil target and the real selector once the bar exists.

`on_action` is where the host says what an action means. kavacha builds
no JavaScript: a library that packages somebody else’s app does not know
the name of their dispatch function.
[`run`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/build.html#run) is
separate because a
[`Js`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#js) row is
JavaScript by definition, and defaults to
[`_menu_run`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#_menu_run)
against the focused window.

### install_menu_patch

``` python
def install_menu_patch(
    specs, lookup
):
```

*Finish each item off as AppKit needs it, wherever pywebview builds the
bar.*

It rebuilds on every focus change to a window whose menu differs, so
anything done once to the bar after start is thrown away. This wraps the
one method both rebuild paths go through.

pywebview rebuilds the whole menu bar whenever the focused window’s menu
differs from the one it built last, so anything done to the bar once,
after start, is thrown away at the next focus change.
[`install_menu_patch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#install_menu_patch)
wraps `_recreate_menus`, the one method both rebuild paths go through,
and every rebuilt bar is decorated again.

It patches once. A second call returns False and changes nothing. So
does a call where pywebview’s cocoa backend will not import.

`specs` is captured by the wrapper, so the table
[`menu_bar`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#menu_bar)
returned is the table every later rebuild uses.

[`_decorate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#_decorate)
finishes the rows AppKit has to finish. A
[`Std`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#std) row is
given a nil target and its selector, which is what walks the responder
chain and lets Cut, Copy, Paste and Minimize reach the web view. Every
other row is given the chord
[`menu_chord`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#menu_chord)
allows it. A row with no entry in `specs` is left alone.

The Window menu is handed to `NSApp` as the windows menu, which is what
puts the open windows on it.

[`_decorate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#_decorate)
runs inside the wrapper
[`install_menu_patch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#install_menu_patch)
installed, and every exception it raises is caught there. A bar that
cannot be decorated is a bar without chords, not a failed launch.
